To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mutations in the genes encoding the subunits of the K+ channel were not predictive of outcome of therapy with diazoxide or other drugs in PHHI patients.
mutations in ABCC8 gene are not predictive of the therapeutic response to diazoxide or other drugs.
mutations in the genes of the K+ channels were not predictive of response to drugs in PHHI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the correlation of the molecular genetic abnormalities in the K+ ATP channel and the response to therapy in patients with PHII.
the identification of mutations in the genes encoding the subunits of the K+ ATP channel in PHHI.
mutations of KATP channels in PHHI
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the outcome of therapeutic modalities in PHHI is not predictable from the mutations of the genes for K+ATP.
mutations in the genes for the subunits that make up the K+ATPs are associated with PHHI and the response to diazoxide is not predictable from the presence or absence of these mutations.
there is no correlation between the mutations in the KATP channel subunits ABCC8 and/or KCNJ11 and the outcome of the therapeutic measures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ABCC8 mutations are not the only cause of hyperinsulinism and that the mutations in the ABBC8 gene are not necessarily the cause of unresponsiveness to drugs.
mutations in the KATP channels do not predict response to diazoxide or other drugs.
the mutations in the ABBC8 gene are associated with the severity of the disease and the response to the therapy but not with the response to surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not the mutation itself, but its effect on the channel function that determines the outcome of the therapy.
in the presence of a mutation in the ABCC 8 gene, the patient may not respond to diazoxide.
the mutations identified in the KATP channel are not predictive of the therapeutic response to diazoxide and that the outcome of therapy with diazoxide is unpredictable.
